recognize_zh: 中央的幼紅血球體積大，細胞質已呈灰粉紅色（已有血紅素），但核仍大而染色質呈疏鬆、篩孔狀（sieve-like），核質發育不同步（nuclear-cytoplasmic asynchrony），符合巨母紅血球性幼紅血球（megaloblastic erythroid precursor）。
features: Markedly enlarged erythroid precursor, several times the diameter of adjacent red cells
Large round nucleus with open, finely stippled sieve-like chromatin despite cytoplasmic maturity
Abundant gray-pink partially hemoglobinized cytoplasm (polychromatophilic stage)
Nuclear-cytoplasmic asynchrony: nucleus appears younger than the cytoplasm
Marrow aspirate background with other precursors and red cells
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a markedly enlarged erythroid precursor with abundant gray-pink, partially hemoglobinized cytoplasm. The nucleus is large and round with open, finely granular sieve-like chromatin, which is immature relative to the degree of cytoplasmic hemoglobinization. Other hematopoietic precursors are present at the periphery of the field. Findings are consistent with a megaloblastic erythroid precursor showing nuclear-cytoplasmic asynchrony, as seen in vitamin B12 or folate deficiency, drug effect, or dyserythropoiesis.

ddx.vs: A normal polychromatophilic normoblast is smaller with a condensed, coarsely clumped nucleus appropriate to its hemoglobinized cytoplasm.
MDS megaloblastoid precursors look similar but occur with normal B12/folate and other dysplastic features (ring sideroblasts, dysgranulopoiesis, abnormal megakaryocytes).
Plasma cells have an eccentric nucleus with clock-face chromatin, deep blue cytoplasm and a perinuclear hof rather than gray-pink hemoglobinized cytoplasm.
Pure erythroid leukemia shows sheets of deeply basophilic, often vacuolated proerythroblasts comprising at least 80% of marrow cells, not isolated maturing megaloblastic cells.
